---
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Let $g \ge 1$ be a natural number and $\mathbf{g} := \{ g_i \}_{i = 1}^m$ be a partition of $g$. We say that an abelian variety $A$ of dimension $g$ over a field $k$ is \textbf{(prime-to-$p$) of splitting type} $\mathbf{g}$ if there exists a set of abelian varieties $A_j$ with $\dim A_j = g_j$ and a prime-to-$p$ isogeny $\prod_{j = 1}^m A_j \to A$. Moreover, we define 
    \begin{equation}
    \label{deltaeq}
    \delta(\mathbf{g}) = \frac{g(g + 1)}{2} - \sum_{j = 1}^m \frac{g_j(g_j + 1)}{2}, 
    \end{equation}
    i.e., the codimension of the image of $\prod_{j = 1}^m \mathsf{A}_{g_j}$ in $\mathsf{A}_g$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm: main density}
    Suppose that $\mathbf{g}$ is a partition of $g \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\delta(\mathbf{g}) < 3g - 3$. Then there exists $r_\mathbf{g} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every prime $p > r_\mathbf{g}$, the locus 
    \begin{equation}
         \mathrm{SP}_{\mathbf{g}, p} := \{ s \in \mathsf{M}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p} : \mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{C}_s) \textit{ is prime-to-$p$ of splitting type } \mathbf{g} \}
    \end{equation}
    is Zariski dense in $\mathsf{M}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p}$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj: AIM}
    \emph{(AIM)} Let $\mathscr{S}$ denote the canonical integral model of a Shimura variety with reflex field $E$, $X, Y$ be generically ordinary irreducible subvarieties of $\mathscr{S}_{k(v)}$, where $v$ is a prime of good reduction with residue characteristic $p$, and suppose that
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eqn: dim condition}
        \dim X + \dim Y \ge \dim \mathscr{S}_{k(v)}. 
    \end{equation}
    Then the set $\{ (x, y) \in X \times Y : x \in \cup_T T(y) \}$ is Zariski dense in $X \times Y$, where $T$ runs through the prime-to-$p$ Hecke operators.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{cubicthreefoldthm}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be the moduli space of smooth cubic threefolds over $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})$, and let $\mathcal{X}$ be the universal family over $\mathsf{M}$. Then there exists an $r$ such that for all $p > r$, the locus 
    \begin{equation}
    \label{cubicspliteq}
        \{ s \in \mathsf{M}_{\mathbb{F}_p} : \mathrm{IJ}(\mathcal{X}_s) \text{ is prime-to-$p$ of splitting type } (1, 1, 1, 1, 1) \}
    \end{equation}
    is Zariski dense in $\mathsf{M}_{\mathbb{F}_p}$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
\emph{(Oort)}
    \label{ques: Oort} Let $\mathsf{A}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{ss}}$ be the supersingular locus of $\mathsf{A}_g$ and let $\tau : \mathsf{M}_g^\mathrm{ct} \to \mathsf{A}_g$ be the Torelli morphism. What is the dimension of $\tau(\mathsf{M}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p}^\mathrm{ct}) \cap \mathsf{A}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{ss}}$?
<!-- end question-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm: Oort}
    When $g \ge 16$, the union over all primes 
    $$ \bigcup_{p \in \mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})} [\tau(\mathsf{M}^\mathrm{ct}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p}) \cap \mathsf{A}^{\mathrm{ss}}_{g, \mathbb{F}_p}]^{> 0} $$
    \textit{is not Zariski dense in $\tau(\mathsf{M}_g^\mathrm{ct})$.} Moreover, the image in $\mathsf{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}}$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-fiber of the Zariski closure of this union lands inside finitely many strict Shimura subvarieties of $\mathsf{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}}$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{orthogonalssthm} \emph{(\cref{preciseorthogonalshimurasupsingthm})}
    Let $\mathscr{S}(L)$ be an integral model over $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$ of an orthogonal Shimura variety associated to a quadratic lattice $L$ of signature $(2, b)$. Let $T$ be a smooth scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$, quasi-finite over $\mathscr{S}(L)$, and such that the image of $T_\mathbb{C}$ has Zariski dense monodromy. Write $\mathscr{S}^{\mathrm{ss}, \sigma_0}_{\mathbb{F}_p}$ for the supersingular locus with Artin invariant $\sigma_0$. Then the union of positive-dimensional atypical components 
    $$ \bigcup_{p \in \mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z}[1/N])} [T_{\mathbb{F}_p} \cap \mathscr{S}^{\mathrm{ss}, \sigma_0}_{\mathbb{F}_p}]^{\mathrm{atyp}, >0} $$
    is not Zariski dense in $T$, and the $\mathbb{C}$-fiber of the Zariski closure of this union is contained in a finite union of Shimura subvarieties strictly contained in $\mathscr{S}(L)_{\mathbb{C}}$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- question-2: body_md -->
\emph{(de Jong)} Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that there is a 1-parameter family of supersingular quintic surfaces of characteristic $p$?
<!-- end question-2 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{supsingquintic}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be the open substack of $|\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(5)| / \mathrm{PGL}_4$ parametrizing smooth quintics. Then there exists a strict Zariski closed substack $Z \subset \mathsf{M}$, with $Z_{\mathbb{C}}$ a finite union of special subloci, such that on $\mathsf{M} \smallsetminus Z$ there are only finitely many primes $p$ for which there exists a one-parameter family of $p$-torsion supersingular quintics.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
As de Jong observed, the only explicitly known example of a positive-dimensional family of supersingular quintics is the one defined by Shioda, when $p = 5$, that is, 
    \begin{equation}
    \label{eqn: Shioda}
        X_0^5 = F(X_1, X_2, X_3)
    \end{equation}
    for a general quintic homogeneous form $F$ (see also \cref{rmk: singular quintic}). We note that these surfaces are indeed $5$-torsion: (\ref{eqn: Shioda}) defines a singular quintic with 13 $A_4$ singularities (\cite[Thm.~1.2]{Bla85}). Then the Tate module $T$ of the resolution is given by 13 copies of the $A_4$ root lattice (after tensoring with $\mathbb{Z}_p$), plus the Chern class of the polarization.
    
    The atypical locus $Z_{\mathbb{C}}$ is needed to allow for the possibility of ``type I constructions'' --- that is, constructions making use of extra geometry present along special subvarieties --- as happened for curves. Without a more precise understanding of this atypical locus, we believe a statement like that appearing in \autoref{supsingquintic} is ``as good as it gets''.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{genericflatnessMg}
Let $L$ be a number field and $N \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a non-zero integer. Let $\varphi : T \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ be a quasi-finite morphism of Deligne-Mumford stacks over $\mathcal{O}_{L}[1/N]$, with $T$ smooth over $\mathcal{O}_{L}[1/N]$, and such that $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}$ has Hodge-generic image. Then after possibly increasing $N$, there exists a strict Zariski closed locus $E \subsetneq T$ with the following property: for every morphism of (integral canonical models of) Shimura varieties $w : Y \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ such that
\[ \dim \varphi(T_{\mathbb{C}}) + \dim Y_{\mathbb{C}} \geq \dim \mathsf{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}} \]
the restriction $(\varphi^{*} Y)^{\circ}$ of $\varphi^{*} Y$ to the fibre above $T - E$ is syntomic (i.e., flat and lci) over $\mathcal{O}_{L}[1/N]$. Moreover $E_{\mathbb{C}}$ is a union of special loci of $T_{\mathbb{C}}$, and each non-empty fibre of $(\varphi^{*} Y)^{\circ} \to \mathrm{Spec}\, \mathcal{O}_{L}[1/N]$ has expected dimension
\[ \dim \varphi(T_{\mathbb{C}}) + \dim Y_{\mathbb{C}} - \dim \mathsf{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}} . \]
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{liftisodecompthm}
Outside the locus $E \subsetneq \mathsf{M}_{g}$ of \autoref{genericflatnessMg}, the following holds: for every partition $\mathbf{g} := \{ g_i \}_{i = 1}^m$ with $\delta(\mathbf{g}) \leq 3g-3$ (recall \eqref{deltaeq}), if $[C] \in \mathsf{M}_{g}(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p})$ is a curve such that $J(C)$ admits a prime-to-$p$ splitting of type $\mathbf{g}$, then $[C]$ lifts to a point $[\widetilde{C}] \in \mathsf{M}_{g}(R)$ together with the splitting, with $R$ finite over $W(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p})$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{isogenyliftthm}
Fix an integer $g \leq 9$. Then there exists a strict closed locus $E \subsetneq \mathsf{M}_{g} \times \mathsf{M}_{g}$ with the following property: for every point $([C], [C']) \in (\mathsf{M}_{g} \times \mathsf{M}_{g} - E)(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p})$ and prime-to-$p$ isogeny $\beta : J(C) \to J(C')$, there exists a finite extension $R$ of $W(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p})$ and lifts $(\widetilde{C}, \widetilde{C}', \widetilde{\beta})$ to $R$ of the data $(C, C', \beta)$. Moreover $E_{\mathbb{C}}$ is a union of special subvarieties.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rmk: effectivity}
    All atypical loci --- that is all the loci labelled ``$E$'' in the theorems in both this and the prior sections --- are constructed effectively using an explicit algebro-geometric procedure. This ultimately reduces to effective procedures for computing the filtered vector bundles with connection $(\mathcal{H}, F^{\bullet}, \nabla)$ coming from algebraic de Rham cohomology, as well as the explicit construction of the maps $\eta^{d}_{r}$ in \autoref{bigjetthm} using this data. For more details see the discussion in \cite[\S1.3]{zbMATH08159582}.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- notn-1: body_md -->
\label{disknot}
Let $k$ be a field together with a map $R \to k$, and $s \in T(k)$ a point. Then we set $\Delta^{r}_{s} := \mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_{T_k, s}/\mathfrak{m}^{r+1})$, where $\mathfrak{m} \subset \mathcal{O}_{T_{k}, s}$ is the maximal ideal corresponding to $s$.
<!-- end notn-1 -->
<!-- notn-2: body_md -->
For a vector space $V$ over a field $k$, we write $\textrm{Fr}(V)$ for the set of frames (bases) of $V$.
<!-- end notn-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{trivlem}
Let $k, s, \Delta^{r}_{s}$ be as in \autoref{disknot}. Then every basis $b^{\bullet} = (b^{1}, \hdots, b^{m}) \in \textrm{Fr}(\mathcal{H}_s)$ induces a unique horizontal trivialization $i_{b^{\bullet}} : {
	\left.\kern-\nulldelimiterspace
	(\mathcal{H}, \nabla)
	\vphantom{\big|}
	\right|_{\Delta^r_s}
	} \xrightarrow{\sim} (\mathcal{O}_{\Delta^r_s}, d)^{\oplus m}$ whose induced map $\mathcal{H}_s \to k^{m}$ is the one induced by $b^{\bullet}$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
This is \cite[Lem. A.0.1]{zbMATH08159582}, where we note that $r!$ is invertible in $k$ because it is so in $R$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{rlimpdef}
Let $k, s, \Delta^{r}_s$ be as in \autoref{trivlem}. An $r$'th order local infinitesimal period map ($r$-limp) is a morphism $\Delta^{r}_s \to \widecheck{L}_k$ corresponding to the filtration $i_{b^{\bullet}}(\textrm{Fil}^{\bullet})$ for some choice of basis $b^{\bullet}$ for $\mathcal{H}_{s}$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{bigjetthm}
There exists a $\mathrm{GL}_{m, R}$-equivariant morphism $\alpha^d_r : \mathcal{P}^d_r \to J^d_r \widecheck{L}$ whose induced map on $k$-points, for each field $k$ admitting a map $R \to k$, is the map $\alpha^d_r(k)$ described above. The resulting morphism 
\[ \eta^{d}_{r} : J^{d}_{r} T \to \mathrm{GL}_{m, R} \backslash J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{L} \]
of Artin stacks over $R$ is compatible with 
\begin{itemize}
\item[-] base-change along maps $R \to R'$ of $\mathbb{Z}[1/r!]$-algebras;
\item[-] pullback along maps $g : T' \to T$ of smooth $R$-schemes, in the sense that $\eta^{d}_{r} \circ J^{d}_{r} g$ is the map associated to $(g^{*} \mathcal{H}, g^{*} \mathrm{Fil}^{\bullet}, g^{*} \nabla)$; and
\item[-] maps of functors $J^{d}_{r} \to J^{d'}_{r'}$ for $r' \leq r$ induced by maps $\mathbb{D}^{d'}_{r',R} \to \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,R}$, in the sense that the natural square involving $J^{d}_{r} T, J^{d'}_{r'} T, \mathrm{GL}_{m} \backslash J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{L}$ and $\mathrm{GL}_{m} \backslash J^{d'}_{r'} \widecheck{L}$ commutes. 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- construction-1: body_md -->
\label{gentorsorconstr} We define
\begin{equation}
\label{Hotimes}
\mathcal{H}^{\otimes} := \bigoplus_{a, b \geq 0} \mathcal{H}^{\otimes a} \otimes (\mathcal{H}^{\vee})^{\otimes b}
\end{equation}
to be the infinite dimensional vector bundle obtained by summing all tensor powers of $\mathcal{H}$ and its dual. The vector bundle $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes}$ has a natural filtration and connection we again denote by $(\textrm{Fil}^{\bullet}, \nabla)$. If one considers the global sections $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes}(T)$, there is a natural $R$-submodule $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes}(T)^{\nabla = 0}$ which consists of exactly the flat global sections.

After replacing $L$ with a finite extension and increasing $N$, we can assume that $T$ admits an $R$-point $t$. We fix an isomorphism $\mathcal{H}_{t} \cong R^{m}$, the choice of which does not matter. Via this isomorphism, the frame bundle $\mathcal{P} := \mathcal{P}^{0}_{0}$ of $\mathcal{H}$ is identified with the principal bundle of isomorphisms associated to the sheaf $\mathcal{F} := \operatorname{\mathscr{H}\text{\kern -3pt {\calligra\large om}}\,}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{O}_{T} \otimes_{R} \mathcal{H}_{t})$. Under this identification, $\mathcal{P}$ is an open subscheme of the relative spectrum (cf. \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LQ}{Section 01LQ}]{stacks-project})
\[ \mathcal{P} \subset \underline{Spec}_{T}(\textrm{Sym}(\mathcal{F})) \]
which is characterized by the property that its points correspond to invertible linear maps. We define a closed subscheme of $\mathcal{P}$ by defining a closed subscheme of $\underline{Spec}_{T}(\textrm{Sym}(\mathcal{F}))$ and then intersecting. More precisely, we can, for each global section $h$ of $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes}$, consider the locus
\[ \mathcal{Z}(h) \subset \underline{Spec}_{T}(\textrm{Sym}(\mathcal{F})) \]
defined by the property that $(s, \varphi) \in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal{H}_{s}, \mathcal{H}_{t})$ lies in $\mathcal{Z}(h)$ if $\varphi(h_{s}) = \varphi(h_{t})$.  Using explicit coordinates for $\underline{Spec}_{T}(\textrm{Sym}(\mathcal{F}))$ one can observe this is a closed locus, and define
\[ \mathcal{M} := \mathcal{P} \cap \bigcap_{h \in \mathcal{H}^{\otimes}(T)^{\nabla = 0}} \mathcal{Z}(h) .\]

We let $\mathbf{H}_{t} \subset \mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{H}_{t})$ be the $R$-subgroup scheme defined as the stabilizer of $[\mathcal{H}^{\otimes}(T)^{\nabla = 0}]_{t}$.
<!-- end construction-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
After possibly increasing $N$, $\mathcal{M}$ is an $\mathbf{H}_{t}$-torsor in the \'etale topology on $T$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We first observe that the complex analytification $\mathcal{M}^{\textrm{an}}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is an $\mathbf{H}_{t,\mathbb{C}}$-torsor in the usual sense of topology. This one can check locally, so we can fix an open neighbourhood $B \subset T(\mathbb{C})$ and check everything after restricting all the data to $B$. In this case we can assume that $\mathcal{H}$ is trivialized by a flat frame, in which case $\mathcal{M}$ is identified with a trivial torsor of the form $B \times \mathbf{H}_{t} \to B$ and the result follows. 

Now we consider the statement of the lemma for $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}$. It follows from the complex analytic version that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}} \to T$ is flat and of finite presentation. Considering the trivialization $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}} \times \mathbf{H}_{t,\mathbb{C}} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}} \times_{T_{\mathbb{C}}} \mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}$ given on points by $((\beta, s), \gamma) \mapsto ((\beta, s), (\gamma \circ \beta, s))$, one also sees that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is an fppf torsor. But any fppf torsor is an \'etale torsor \cite{51051}. The statement likewise follows for $\mathcal{M}_{L}$.

Having shown the statement for $\mathcal{M}_{L}$, choose an \'etale map $U \to T$ such that $\mathcal{M}_{L} \times_{T} U \to U$ is trivial. Choosing $N$ large enough the trivialization spreads out, hence so does the torsor structure.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Using the identification $\mathcal{H}_{t} \cong R^{m}$, we define $\widecheck{D}_{\textrm{mon}} \subset \widecheck{L}$ to be the locally closed subscheme of $\widecheck{L}$ obtained as the orbit of $\mathbf{H}_{t}$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Using the identification $\mathcal{H}_{t} \cong R^{m}$, we define $\widecheck{D}_{\textrm{Hg}} \subset \widecheck{L}$ to be the closed subscheme consisting of those flags $F^{\bullet}$ such that $h_{t}$ lies in the middle piece of $F^{\bullet}$ for all $h \in \mathcal{H}^{{\otimes}}(T)^{\nabla = 0}$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
Suppose that the data $(\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{C}}, \mathrm{Fil}^{\bullet}_{\mathbb{C}}, \nabla_{\mathbb{C}})$ underlies a polarized $\mathbb{Q}$-variation of pure Hodge structures $\mathbb{V}$, and that $\mathbf{H}_{t,\mathbb{C}}$ is connected. Then the locus $\widecheck{D}_{\operatorname{Hg}, \mathbb{C}}$ is a finite union of $\mathbf{H}_{t,\mathbb{C}}$ orbits, one of which is $\widecheck{D}_{\operatorname{mon}, \mathbb{C}}$. Consequently, after possibly increasing $N$ and replacing $L$ with a finite extension, $\widecheck{D}_{\operatorname{Hg}}$ is a finite union of $\mathbf{H}_{t}$ orbits, one of which is $\widecheck{D}_{\operatorname{mon}}$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
In what follows we set $\widecheck{D} = \widecheck{D}_{\textrm{Hg}}$ for convenience. To start with we replace $R$ with $\mathbb{C}$, and in particular regard $t$ as a $\mathbb{C}$-point. Then the fibre $\mathcal{H}_{t}$, the algebraic group $\mathbf{H}_{t}$, and the varieties $\widecheck{D}$ and $\widecheck{L}$ are all complex-algebraic. The fibre $\mathbb{V}_{t}$ then gives a $\mathbb{Q}$-structure for the complex vector space $\mathcal{H}_{t}$ and the algebraic group $\mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{H}_{t})$, and under our identifications a $\mathbb{Q}$-structure for the flag variety $\widecheck{L}$. We denote the resulting $\mathbb{Q}$-varieties by $\mathcal{H}_{t,\mathbb{Q}}$, $\mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{H}_{t,\mathbb{Q}})$ and $\widecheck{L}_{\mathbb{Q}}$, respectively. Likewise, one has an infinite rank local system $\mathbb{V}^{\otimes} = \bigoplus_{a, b \geq 0} \mathbb{V}^{\otimes a} \otimes (\mathbb{V}^{\vee})^{\otimes b}$ which underlies the bundle $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes}$ from (\ref{Hotimes}). This then equips $W := \mathcal{H}^{\otimes}(T)^{\nabla = 0}$ with a $\mathbb{Q}$-structure $W_{\mathbb{Q}}$, and hence gives us a $\mathbb{Q}$-structure $\mathbf{H}_{t,\mathbb{Q}}$ for the group $\mathbf{H}_{t}$ which is the pointwise stabilizer of this subspace. It now suffices to give an alternative construction of $\widecheck{D}$ using this $\mathbb{Q}$-structure such that $\widecheck{D}$ is a finite union of $\mathbf{H}_{t}(\mathbb{C})$-orbits. 

The subspace $W_{\mathbb{Q}}$ has a natural subspace $W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ consisting of those vectors which are everywhere Hodge for the filtration $\mathrm{Fil}^{\bullet}$. We can consider the fibre $[W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q}}]_{t}$ of $W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ at $t$, or alternatively, we can consider the subspace $W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q},t} \subset W_{\mathbb{Q},t}$ of the fibre of $W_{\mathbb{Q}}$ at $t$ consisting of those $w \in W_{\mathbb{Q},t}$ such that $w$ is Hodge for the Hodge structure at $t$ (but not necessarily globally). We have a natural map $[W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q}}]_{t} \to W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q},t}$, which is an isomorphism as a consequence of Schmid's fixed part theorem \cite{zbMATH03437307}. We therefore drop the distinction between $W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q},t}$ and $[W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q}}]_{t}$.

Let us write $\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{G}_{t} \subset \mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{H}_{t,\mathbb{Q}})$ for the algebraic group defined as the pointwise stabilizer of $W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q},t}$. Write $h_{t} : \mathbb{S} \to \mathrm{GL}(\mathbb{V}_{t})$ for the Hodge structure at $t$, and write $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{G}} \subset \widecheck{L}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic subvariety defined by the property that a flag $F^{\bullet} \in \widecheck{L}(\mathbb{C})$ lies inside $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{G}}$ if and only if each element of $W^{\textrm{Hg}}_{\mathbb{Q},t}$ is Hodge for $F^{\bullet}$ (lies in the middle step of the filtration on the appropriate tensor space). Then the following facts are known about the relationships between the above data: 
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] as a consequence of \cite[Thm. 1]{zbMATH00060857} the group $\mathbf{H}_{t}$ is a normal subgroup of the derived subgroup of $\mathbf{G}$;
    \item[(ii)] by \cite[VI.B.1]{zbMATH06031035} each component of $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{G}}$ is an orbit of $G(\mathbb{C})$; and
    \item[(iii)] there exists $\gamma \in \mathbf{G}(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\gamma \cdot h_{t}$ has Mumford-Tate $\mathbf{M} \subset \mathbf{G}$ whose derived subgroup agrees with $\mathbf{H}_{t}$. 
\end{itemize}
To see (iii) we may argue as follows. First let us write $\widecheck{D}_{\mathbf{G}} \subset \widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{G}}$ for the component containing $h_{t}$. Then applying \cite[III.A]{zbMATH06031035} the orbit $D_{\mathbf{G}} := \mathbf{G}(\mathbb{R}) \cdot h_{t}$ factors as a product $D_{\mathbf{G}} = D_{\mathbf{H}} \times D_{\mathbf{L}}$, with
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{H} \cdot \mathbf{L} \cdot \mathbf{T}$ the almost-direct decomposition of the reductive $\mathbb{Q}$-group $\mathbf{G}$, where $\mathbf{H} = \mathbf{H}_{t}$, $\mathbf{L}$ is the complementary semisimple factor, and $\mathbf{T}$ is the torus part; and
    \item $D_{\mathbf{H}} = \mathbf{H}(\mathbb{R}) \cdot h_{t}$ and $D_{\mathbf{L}} = \mathbf{L}(\mathbb{R}) \cdot h_{t}$. 
\end{itemize}
Now to obtain $\gamma$ as in (iii) we start by choosing $\gamma' \in G(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\gamma' \cdot h_{t}$ is a CM-Hodge structure; this is possible as a consequence of \cite[VI.C.1]{zbMATH06031035} and \cite[VI.A.2]{zbMATH06031035}. Then the map $\gamma' \cdot h_{t} : \mathbb{S} \to \mathbf{G}_{\mathbb{R}}$ factors through some product $\mathbf{T}_{H} \cdot \mathbf{T}_{L} \cdot \mathbf{T}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$-tori compatibly with the decomposition $\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{H} \cdot \mathbf{L} \cdot \mathbf{T}$. It therefore suffices to show that if we take a very general $h \in \mathbf{H}(\mathbb{R})$ and set $\gamma = h \gamma'$, then the Mumford-Tate group of $\gamma \cdot h_{t}$ agrees with $\mathbf{H} \cdot \mathbf{T}_{L} \cdot \mathbf{T}$.

If not, then there must exist a strict $\mathbb{Q}$-subgroup $\mathbf{H}' \subsetneq \mathbf{H}$ which contains the image under the map $\mathbf{G}/(\mathbf{L} \cdot \mathbf{T}) \to \mathbf{H}$ of a very general element of $D_{\mathbf{H}}$, and hence of $D_{\mathbf{G}}$. But that would imply that a very general element of $D_{\mathbf{G}}$ has Mumford-Tate group strictly contained in $\mathbf{G}$, which is not true (take the Mumford-Tate group associated to a very general point in our base $T(\mathbb{C})$). We have thus shown (iii) above.

                                                                                                                                                                                               

Below we write $V$ for $\mathbb{V}_t$. 
Now let $w_{1}, \hdots, w_{r} \in \bigoplus_{a, b \geq 0} V^{\otimes a} \otimes (V^{\vee})^{\otimes b}$ be a collection of Hodge tensors such that $\mathbf{M}$ is exactly the pointwise stabilizer of $w_{1}, \hdots, w_{r}$. Write $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}} \subset \widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{G}}$ for the locus of Hodge flags for which the $w_{1}, \hdots, w_{r}$ are Hodge tensors. Then again by \cite[VI.B.1]{zbMATH06031035} each component of $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$, and in particular the component containing $\gamma \cdot h_{t}$, is a $\mathbf{M}(\mathbb{C})$-orbit. Since the torus part of $\mathbf{M}$ acts trivially on the components of $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$, all of which are proper algebraic varieties, it follows that each component of $\widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$, and in particular the component containing $\gamma \cdot h_{t}$, is a $\mathbf{H}_{t}(\mathbb{C})$-orbit. 

If we now consider the locus $\gamma^{-1} \widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$, then because $\gamma$ commutes with $\mathbf{H}_{t}(\mathbb{C})$ its components are also $\mathbf{H}_{t}(\mathbb{C})$-orbits. Moreover $\gamma^{-1} \widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$ is the locus of flags for which the complex tensors $\gamma^{-1} w_{1}, \hdots, \gamma^{-1} w_{r}$ are ``Hodge'' (lie in the middle piece of the appropriate filtration on the associated tensor space). If we construct a period map as in \cite[III.A]{zbMATH06031035} by choosing $t$ as our basepoint, then the lifted period map $\widetilde{T}_{\mathbb{C}} \to \widecheck{L}$ will factor through $D_{\mathbf{H}} \subset \gamma^{-1} \widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$, and so it follows that the $\gamma^{-1} w_{1}, \hdots, \gamma^{-1} w_{r}$ induced global Hodge tensors of the complex local system $\mathbb{V}_{\mathbb{C}}$; in particular, one obtains the equality $\widecheck{D} = \gamma^{-1} \widecheck{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathbf{M}}$, completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- construction-2: body_md -->
\label{constr: functoriality of pair}
    The pair $(H := \mathbf{H}_t, \widecheck{D})$ is functorial in the pointed space $(T, t)$ in the following sense. Suppose that $T' \to T$ is a morphism of $R$-schemes and $t' \in T'(R)$ is a base point of $T'$. Then we can form $(H', \widecheck{D}')$ over $T'$ using the restriction $\mathcal{H}|_{T'}$. Viewing $t'$ as an $R$-point on $T$, we may consider the $H$-orbit of the isomorphism $\varphi : \mathcal{H}_{t'} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} \mathcal{H}_t$ inside the torsor $\mathcal{M}$. Using $\varphi$, we obtain an embedding $(H', \widecheck{D}') \hookrightarrow (H, \widecheck{D})$. Note that the orbit of the embedding under the $H$-action on $(H, \widecheck{D})$ (via $\gamma \cdot (h, F^\bullet) = (\gamma h \gamma^{-1}, \gamma F^\bullet)$) depends only on the morphism $T' \to T$ and not on the choice of $t'$ and $\varphi$.
<!-- end construction-2 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{refinedjetthm}
The map $\alpha^{d}_{r} : \mathcal{P}^{d}_{r} \to J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{L}$ from \autoref{bigjetthm} above restricts to give a map $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r} \to J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{D}$. In particular we obtain a map of Artin stacks
\[ \eta^{d}_{r} : J^{d}_{r} T \to \mathbf{H}_{t} \backslash J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{D} \]
over $R$, compatible with base-change along maps $R \to R'$ of $\mathbb{Z}[1/r!]$-algebras, and functorial in maps of functors $J^{d}_{r} \to J^{d'}_{r'}$ for $r' \leq r$ induced by maps $\mathbb{D}^{d'}_{r',R} \to \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,R}$. When $k$ is a field admitting a map from $R$, the description of the map on $k$-points is given by $(j, \varphi) \mapsto \psi \circ j$, where $\psi$ is the $r$-limp $\Delta^{r}_{s} \to \widecheck{L}_{k}$ of \autoref{rlimpdef}. The map $\psi$ factors through $\widecheck{D}_{k}$ by construction.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
It suffices to prove that the restriction of $\alpha^{d}_{r}$ to $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}$ factors through $J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{D}$, since the rest follows from \autoref{bigjetthm}. Applying the base-change compatibility of the construction one can reduce to checking this on closed points, where it reduces to showing that $r$-limps $\psi$ factor through $\widecheck{D}$. Using the fact that $\widecheck{D}$ is a component of $\widecheck{D}_{\operatorname{Hg}}$, this reduces to the claim that if $\widetilde{\varphi} \in \operatorname{\mathscr{H}\text{\kern -3pt {\calligra\large om}}\,}({
	\left.\kern-\nulldelimiterspace
	\mathcal{H}
	\vphantom{\big|}
	\right|_{\Delta^{r}_{s}}
	}, \mathcal{O}_{\Delta^{r}_{s}} \otimes_{k} \mathcal{H}_{t})$ is a flat extension of some $\varphi : \mathcal{H}_{s} \to \mathcal{H}_{t,k}$, then $\widetilde{\varphi}(h)$ is constant for each $h \in \mathcal{H}^{\otimes}(T)^{\nabla = 0}$. This can be checked directly using the fact that $h$ is flat.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- setup-1: body_md -->
\label{setup base}
    Let $R = \mathcal{O}_L[1/N]$, fix an embedding $\iota : L \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$. Let $T$ be a smooth $R$-scheme with a base point $t \in T(R)$. Let $(\mathcal{H}, \mathrm{Fil}^\bullet, \nabla)$ be a filtered flat vector bundle on $T$ such that its $\mathbb{C}$-fiber underlies a polarizable $\mathbb{Z}$-VHS $\mathbb{V}$. Assume that $t_\mathbb{C}$ is Hodge-generic and set $G := \mathrm{MT}(\mathbb{V}_{t_\mathbb{C}})$. The group $G$ is reductive; let $G_{1}, \hdots, G_{k}$ be its $\mathbb{Q}$-simple factors. Assume that $G$ (resp. $G_i$ for $i = 1, \cdots, k$) spreads out to a smooth reductive group scheme $\mathbf{G}_t$ (resp. $\mathbf{G}_{i, t}$). Then after reordering there exists $j \leq k$ such that $\mathbf{G}_{1,t} \cdots \mathbf{G}_{j,t} = \mathbf{H}_{t}$. We have a corresponding decomposition $\widecheck{D} = \widecheck{D}_{1} \times \cdots \times \widecheck{D}_{j}$.
<!-- end setup-1 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
For a scheme $X$ and integers $d, r \geq 0$, we write $J^{d}_{r,c} X \subset J^d_r X$ for the closed subscheme of constant jets, and $J^{d}_{r,\operatorname{nc}} X \subset J^{d}_{r} X$ for the complementary open subscheme of non-constant jets, defined as in \cite[\S3]{urbanik2023algebraiccyclelociintegral}.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- construction-3: body_md -->
\label{constr: atypical E}
\emph{(Atypical locus)}
In \cref{setup base}, we now fix a closed $R$-subscheme $Z \subset \widecheck{D}$ which is geometrically irreducible over $R$ and has relative dimension $e > 0$ over $R$ and do the following constructions. Let $I^c_{Z} \subset \{ 1, \hdots, j \}$ be the subset defined by the property that $Z \to \widecheck{D}_{i}$ is constant for $i \in I^c_Z$, and let $I^\mathrm{nc}_{Z} \subset \{ 1, \hdots, j \}$ be its complement. Accordingly, we set $\widecheck{D}^c_Z := \prod_{i \in I^c_Z} \widecheck{D}_i$ and $\widecheck{D}^\mathrm{nc}_Z := \prod_{i \in I_Z^\mathrm{nc}} \widecheck{D}_i$. Let $\pi_{c} : \widecheck{D} \to \widecheck{D}^{c}_{Z}$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{nc}} : \widecheck{D} \to \widecheck{D}^{\mathrm{nc}}_{Z}$ be the two projections. Define $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z) \subset \mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}$ to be the inverse image of $J^{d}_{r} Z$. Here is a commutative diagram that summarizes the situation: 
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{M}^d_r(Z)} & {\mathcal{M}^d_r} & {J^d_r T} \\
	{J^d_r Z} & {J^d_r \widecheck{D}} & {J^d_r \widecheck{D}^\mathrm{nc}_Z } \\
	& {J^d_r \widecheck{D}_Z^c }
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{{\alpha^d_r}}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\textrm{constant}}"', from=2-1, to=3-2]
	\arrow[from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-2, to=3-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           

We then define, for each $r \geq \xi$, the locus $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z, \xi) \subset \mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z)$ to be the open subscheme obtained by intersecting the following two open conditions (recall the notion of non-degenerate and non-constant jets in \cref{subsec: jets}):
\begin{equation}
\label{cond: nd}
\begin{cases}
    \textrm{the locus $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z, \xi)$ lies above $J^d_{r,nd} T$, which is open in $J^d_r T$; } \\
    \textrm{the locus $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z, \xi)$ lies above $J^d_{\xi, \mathrm{nc}} \widecheck{D}_{i}$ for each $i \in I^{\operatorname{nc}}_{Z}$, which is open in $J^d_\xi \widecheck{D}_{i}$. } 
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Finally, fix some $\xi \in \mathbb{N}$ and for each $d, r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $E^d_r$ be the scheme-theoretic image of the map $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z, \xi) \to T$, and set $E^d := \cap_{r \ge \xi} E^d_r$. Note that since each $E^d_r$ is a closed subscheme by definition, and $T$ is Noetherian, the infinite intersection $\cap_{r \ge \xi} E^d_r$ has to stabilize, i.e., $E^d = E^d_{r_0}$ for $r_0 \gg 0$.
<!-- end construction-3 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def: n(I)}
    In \cref{setup base}, for each subset $I \subset \{ 1, \hdots, j \}$, we define $n(I) \in \mathbb{N}$ to be the dimension of a general non-empty fibre of the composition $B \stackrel{\psi}{\to} \widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C} \to \prod_{i \in I} \widecheck{D}_{i, \mathbb{C}}$, where $\psi : B \to \widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C}$ is any local period map on some ball $B \subset T^{\textrm{an}}_{\mathbb{C}}$. This is easily seen to be independent of $\psi$ and depends only on $I$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{atyplocusconstrprop}
Suppose that in \cref{setup base}, 
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn: d > bla}
    d > n(I_Z^c) -\dim \widecheck{D}^\mathrm{nc}_Z + \dim_{R} Z.
\end{equation}
Then $E^d = E^{d}_{r_{0}}$ is not Zariski dense. If in addition the period map induced by $\mathbb{V}$ has no positive-dimensional fibres, and the algebraic monodromy group $\mathbf{H}_{t}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-simple, then the underlying reduced subscheme of $E^{d}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is contained in a finite union of special subvarieties of $T_{\mathbb{C}}$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{Zatyplocusdef}
When 
\[ d = \max \{ 1, n(I_Z^c) -\dim \widecheck{D}^\mathrm{nc}_Z + \dim_{R} Z + 1 \} , \]
we call the locus $E^{d}_{\mathbb{C}}$ of \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop} the $Z$-atypical locus of $(S_{\mathbb{C}}, \mathbb{V})$. We will sometimes just say ``atypical locus'' when $Z$ is understood.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Note also that by the non-degeneracy condition in (\ref{cond: nd}), for $r \ge 1$ and $d \gg 0$, $E^d_r = \emptyset$. The right hand side of (\ref{eqn: d > bla}) is the ``expected'' dimension of $B \times_{\widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C}, \psi} Z_\mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where $\psi : B \to \widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C}$ is a local period map as in \cref{def: n(I)}. 

Fix some $r_{0} \geq \xi$ and consider the intersection of constructible sets
\[ \mathcal{J}_{r_{0}} = \bigcap_{r \geq r_{0}} \textrm{im}[\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z, \xi) \to \mathcal{M}^{d}_{r_{0}} \times J^{d}_{r_{0}} \widecheck{D}] . \]
Let $(p_{r_{0}}, \sigma_{r_{0}})$ be a $\mathbb{C}$-point in $\mathcal{J}_{r_{0}}$. Set $\mathbb{D}^d_{\infty, \mathbb{C}} := \varinjlim_r \mathbb{D}^d_{r, \mathbb{C}} \simeq \mathrm{Spf}(\mathbb{C}[\![x_1, \cdots, x_d]\!])$. Applying \cite[Lem 5.3]{zbMATH07871772} to the sequence $\{ \mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(Z, \xi) \}_{r \ge r_{0}}$ at the point $(p_{r_{0}}, \sigma_{r_{0}})$ and arguing as in the proof of \cite[Prop. 4.2.5]{zbMATH08159582} we obtain a commutative diagram of formal objects
\begin{equation}
    \begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathbb{D}^d_{\infty, \mathbb{C}}} & {\widehat{S}_s} \\
	{Z_\mathbb{C}} & {\widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C}}
	\arrow["{j_\infty}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\sigma_\infty}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\psi_\infty}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Moreover $j_{\infty}$ is injective on tangent spaces (hence an embedding), and $\sigma_{\infty}$ is non-constant when projected to each $\widecheck{D}_{i}$ where $i \in I^\mathrm{nc}_{Z}$.

The fact that $j_\infty$ is an embedding implies that $\dim (\psi_{\infty})^{-1}(Z_\mathbb{C}) \geq d$. Writing $\Omega' := \widecheck{D}^\mathrm{nc}_Z$ for simplicity, from our assumption (\ref{eqn: d > bla}) on $d$, we have 
\begin{equation}
\label{atypineq}
\dim \Omega' - \dim Z_{\mathbb{C}} > n(I_Z^c) - \dim (\psi_{\infty})^{-1}(Z) .
\end{equation}
Note also that $(\psi_{\infty})^{-1}(Z) \subset (\psi_{\infty})^{-1}(\Omega' \times \{ pt \})$ by construction, and $(\psi_{\infty})^{-1}(\Omega' \times \{ pt \})$ is the germ of a union of weakly special subvarieties $T'$ (i.e., $(\psi_{\infty})^{-1}(\Omega' \times \{ pt \}) = \widehat{T}'_s$) in the sense of \cite[Def.~4.1]{KO21}, which are algebraic by Prop.~4.8 \textit{ibid.} Since the image of $\widehat{T}'_s$ in $\widecheck{D}^c_Z$ is a point, after removing a closed locus from $T$, we may assume that $\dim T' = n(I^c_Z)$. 

Now let $T^{\circ}$ be a component of $T'$ of maximal dimension which factors $j_{\infty}$. Let $\psi^{\circ}_{\infty}$ be the restriction of $\psi_{\infty}$ to the formal completion at $s$ of $T^{\circ}$. Use (\ref{atypineq}) to apply the Ax-Schanuel theorem \cite{zbMATH07066495} to the variation of Hodge structure ${
	\left.\kern-\nulldelimiterspace
	\mathbb{V}
	\vphantom{\big|}
	\right|_{T^{\circ}}
	}$, where we note that $\psi^{-1}_{\infty}(Z) = \psi^{\circ,-1}_{\infty}(Z)$. We learn that $(\psi^{\circ}_{\infty})^{-1}(Z)$ lies in a strict weakly special subvariety $Y \subset T^{\circ}$. If the Mumford-Tate group of $Y$ agrees with that of $T^{\circ}$ then the algebraic monodromy group of $Y$ is normal in the algebraic monodromy group of $T^{\circ}$. But the algebraic monodromy group of $Y$ is a strict subgroup of the algebraic monodromy group of $T^{\circ}$ (since $Y$ is weakly special), so this means in particular that there is some factor $D_{i} \subset \Omega'$ such that the map $\hat{Y}_{s} \to \widecheck{D}_{i}$ induced by $\psi^{\circ}_{\infty}$ is constant. But this cannot happen because $j_{\infty}$ factors through $\hat{Y}_{s}$ and $\sigma_{\infty}$ is non-constant on each such $\widecheck{D}_{i}$ by construction.

It follows that the Mumford-Tate group of $Y$ is strictly contained in the Mumford-Tate group of $T$. By construction this is true for all points in $E^d(\mathbb{C})$ outside of a meagre subset, hence $E^d(\mathbb{C})$ lies inside a finite union of special subvarieties of $T$. This completes the proof of the first statement.

\vspace{0.5em}

                                                                                                 

                                                                                                                                                                                                        

For the claim under the additional $\mathbb{Q}$-simplicity assumption and the assumption on the fibres of the period map, we observe that in this case $j = 1$ and $I_Z^c = \varnothing$. Then $n(I_Z^c) = \dim T_{\mathbb{C}}$ and the step in the above argument where one removes a closed locus from $T$ can be skipped. The proof then shows $E^{d}_{\mathbb{C}}$ lies inside a finite union of special subvarietes of $T$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
Let $(G, X)$ be a Shimura datum of Hodge type and $\mathsf{K} \subseteq G(\mathbb{A}_f)$ be a compact open subgroup small enough such that $\mathrm{Sh}_\mathsf{K}(G, X)$ is a scheme. Given a number field $E \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, we say that $\mathcal{O}_E[1/N]$ is an \textit{admissible base} for $(G, X, \mathsf{K})$ if the following conditions are satisfied: 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape{(\roman*)}]
        \item $E$ contains the reflex field $E(G, X)$; 
        \item $G$ admits a reductive model $\mathcal{G}$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$; 
        \item $\mathsf{K}$ is of the form $\mathsf{K}^N \mathsf{K}_N$, where $\mathsf{K}^N \subseteq G(\mathbb{A}^N_f)$ and $\mathsf{K}_N = \prod_{p \mid N} \mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}_p)$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
This $\mathcal{I}$ is a variant of the $\mathcal{M}$ in \cref{gentorsorconstr}. The only difference is that $\mathcal{I}$ is a $G$-torsor whereas $\mathcal{M}$ would be a $G^{\mathrm{der}}$-torsor.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Applying \cref{setup base}, we let $G_1, \cdots, G_j$ be the $\mathbb{Q}$-simple factors of $G$, and let $\widecheck{D} = \widecheck{D}_{1} \times \cdots \times \widecheck{D}_{j}$ be the usual factorization of $\widecheck{D}$. Note that $j = k$ in this Shimura setting. Then we say that $Z \subset \widecheck{D}$ is factor-transversal if for each non-empty subset $I \subset \{ 1, \hdots, j \}$, the intersection of $Z$ with each fibre of $\widecheck{D} \to \prod_{i \in I} \widecheck{D}_{i}$ is zero-dimensional over $R$.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
Let $(H, \widecheck{D})$ be a pair consisting of a complex algebraic group $H$ and a homogeneous space $\widecheck{D}$ for $H$. Two subvarieties $Z, Z' \subset \widecheck{D}$ are said to be equivalent (relative to $(H, \widecheck{D})$) if for some $h \in H(\mathbb{C})$ we have $h Z = Z'$. An equivalence class is called a \textit{type} (relative to $(H, \widecheck{D})$). If instead $Z$ and $Z'$ are defined over some subring $R \subset \mathbb{C}$, we say that $Z$ and $Z'$ are equivalent (or have the same type) if this is true after base-change to $\mathbb{C}$.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{shimflatnessthmv2}
Let $(G, X)$ be a Hodge-type Shimura datum with level structure $\mathsf{K} \subseteq G(\mathbb{A}_f)$. Let $\mathcal{O}_E[1/N]$ be an admissible base for $(G, X, \mathsf{K})$. Let $T$ be a $\mathscr{S} := \mathscr{S}_\mathsf{K}(G,X)$-scheme which is smooth over $R := \mathcal{O}_{E}[1/N]$ and quasi-finite over $\mathscr{S} := \mathscr{S}_\mathsf{K}(G, X)$, and such that the algebraic monodromy group of $T_{\mathbb{C}}$ agrees with the derived subgroup of $G$. Let $Z \subseteq \widecheck{D} = \widecheck{X}$ be a factor-transversal closed subscheme such that
\[ \dim Z_{\mathbb{C}} + \dim T_{\mathbb{C}} - \dim \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} \geq 0 . \]
Let $E \subset T$ be given by applying \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop} with $(d, \xi)$ as above, increasing $N$ as necessary. Then the following holds: 

Let $(G', X') \subseteq (G, X)$ be a sub-Shimura datum with a level structure $\mathsf{K}' \subseteq G'(\mathbb{A}_f)$ such that $\mathcal{O}_E[1/N]$ remains admissible for $(G', X', \mathsf{K}')$ and $\mathsf{K}' \subseteq \mathsf{K}$. If $\widecheck{X}'$ is of type $Z$, then up to replacing $T$ by its open subscheme $T \smallsetminus E$, the fibre product $T \times_{\mathscr{S}} \mathscr{S}'$ is equidimensional over $R$, and there is no non-degenerate jet $j : \mathbb{D}^d_r \to T \times_{\mathscr{S}} \mathscr{S}'$ defined over any field $k$ over $R$.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $W := \mathscr{S}' \times_\mathscr{S} T$. By replacing $T$ with the open subscheme $T \smallsetminus E$, we may assume without loss of generality that $E = \emptyset$. We aim to show that $W$ is flat over $R$. 

Let $k$ be any algebraically closed field over $R$. For every algebro-geometric point $y \in \mathscr{S}'(k)$ with image $x \in \mathscr{S}$, the induced morphism $(\mathscr{S}'_{W(k)})^\wedge_{y} \to (\mathscr{S}_{W(k)})^\wedge_x$ between the formal completions is a closed embedding which is a local complete intersection of codimension $c = \mathrm{codim}_{\widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C}} Z_\mathbb{C}$.\footnote{One can deduce this from \cite{Xu26}, or simply from \cite[Prop.~2.3.5]{Kis10}.} By base change, we have that if $y$ and $x$ lift to $k$-points of $W$ and $T$, then the morphism between formal completions $(W_{W(k)})^\wedge_y \to (T_{W(k)})^\wedge_x$ is also a closed immersion cut out by $c$ equations. 

By \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00MG}{Tag 00MG}]{stacks-project}, to show that $W$ is flat over $R$, it suffices to show that for every pair of $k$-points $y, x$ on $W, T$ respectively, the special fiber $(W_k)^\wedge_y \hookrightarrow (T_k)^\wedge_x$ has codimension exactly $c$. This can only fail if for some prime $\mathfrak{p} \subset R$ (including the zero prime corresponding to the generic fiber over $L$) and $k = \overline{\kappa(\mathfrak{p})}$, there exists an irreducible component $Y \subseteq W_{k}$ of dimension $d > \dim T_{k} - c$. For the sake of contradiction, assume that such a $Y$ exists. 

Since the Shimura morphism $\mathscr{S}' \to \mathscr{S}$ is unramified, so is $W \to T$ by base change (\cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02GA}{Tag 02GA}]{stacks-project}). This implies that $Y \to T_{k}$ is also unramified by restriction, so that for a general smooth point $y \in Y$, the map $Y \to T_k$ is injective on the tangent space at $y$. For any such smooth point, its local ring $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is regular of dimension $d$, allowing us to construct non-degenerate $d$-dimensional jets $j : \mathbb{D}^d_{r,k} \to Y \to T_k$ for any $r \ge 0$. 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

By construction, these jets factor through $\mathscr{S}'_{k}$, meaning their associated $r$-limps, with $r = r_{0}$, factor through $Z_{k} \subset \widecheck{D}_{k}$ up to the action of $G_{k}$. Letting $\psi$ be an $r$-limp based at $s$, the factor-transversal assumption together with our choice of $\xi$ implies that the jet $\psi \circ j$ is non-constant when projected to each factor of $\widecheck{D}_{k}$. Thus, these jets lift to points in the locus $\mathcal{M}^d_r(Z,\xi)$. Because $d > \dim T - c$, the integer $d$ satisfies the critical dimension inequality (\ref{eqn: d > bla}). Consequently, any such jet lies above the image of $\mathcal{M}^d_r(Z,\xi) \to T$, i.e. in the empty atypical locus $E$.

Therefore, no such $Y$ with dimension larger than $\dim T - c$ can exist, so $W$ is flat over $R$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
The statement can be proven after replacing $\mathsf{A}_{g}$ with a level cover $\mathsf{A}_{g}[n]$, and hence we may assume that $T$ is a scheme with quasi-finite map $\varphi : T \to \mathsf{A}_{g}[n]$ and prove the same statement for this map.

We let $(G, X) = (\mathrm{GSp}_{2g}, \mathbb{H}_{g})$ be the usual Shimura datum associated to the Siegel upper half space, and let $\widecheck{D} = \widecheck{X}$ be the associated sympletic grassmannian of $g$-dimensional Lagrangian subspaces. Then it is well known that, up to equivalence by the $\mathrm{GSp}_{2g}(\mathbb{R})$-action, there are finitely many Shimura subdata $(H, Y) \subset (G,X)$. This implies that we can find finitely many subvarieties $Z_{1}, \hdots, Z_{k} \subset \widecheck{D}$ such that the types of the varieties $\widecheck{Y} \subset \widecheck{X}$ are each represented by one of the $Z_{i}$. We may assume the $Z_{i}$ are defined over $\mathcal{O}_{L'}[1/N]$ with $L'$ a finite extension, enlarging $N$ as necessary.

Now apply \autoref{shimflatnessthmv2} to this situation with $Z = Z_{i}$, and let $E = E_{1} \cup \cdots \cup E_{k}$ be the union of the resulting loci. Then $E$ is defined over $\mathcal{O}_{L'}[1/N]$ (increasing $N$ as necessary), but we may assume it is defined over $\mathcal{O}_{L}[1/N]$ after enlarging $E$ to include the conjugates of the $E_{i}$ over the Galois closure of $L'/L$.

Now the statement of \autoref{shimflatnessthmv2} implies that the fibre products $(T - E) \times_{\mathsf{A}_{g}[n]} Y$ are equidimensional over $R = \mathcal{O}_{L}[1/N]$ of expected codimension $\dim \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} - \dim Z_{i,\mathbb{C}}$, where $i$ depends on $Y$. Each $Y$ is l.c.i. over $\mathsf{A}_{g}[n]$ cut out locally by $\dim \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} - \dim Z_{i,\mathbb{C}}$ functions, so this implies that $(T - E) \times_{\mathsf{A}_{g}[n]} Y$ is likewise l.c.i. over $T - E$. By miracle flatness, each locus $(T - E) \times_{\mathsf{A}_{g}[n]} Y$ is also flat over $R$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
This follows from \autoref{genericflatnessMg} by using the moduli interpretation of the Shimura varieties $w : Y \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ together with the lifting fact \cite[Lem 2.1.5]{zbMATH08159582}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
In this case we take $(G, X) = (\mathrm{GSp}_{2g} \times \mathrm{GSp}_{2g}, \mathbb{H}_{g} \times \mathbb{H}_{g})$, with $\mathrm{GSp}_{2g} = \operatorname{GAut}(V,\omega)$ and $(V,\omega)$ the standard symplectic space, and write $\widecheck{D} = \widecheck{X}$ for the product $\mathrm{IGr}(g, V) \times \mathrm{IGr}(g, V)$ of isotropic Grassmannians. We let $Z \subset \widecheck{D}$ be the diagonally embedded copy of $\mathrm{IGr}(g, V)$. Then $I_Z^c = \varnothing$ (in the language of \autoref{constr: atypical E}), $I^{\operatorname{nc}}_{Z} = \{ 1, 2 \}$ and $\widecheck{D}^\mathrm{nc}_Z := \prod_{i \in I_Z^\mathrm{nc}} \widecheck{D}_i = \widecheck{D}$. We let 
\[ d = n(I_Z^c) - \dim \widecheck{D}^{\operatorname{nc}}_Z + \dim_{R} Z + 1 = 2 \dim_{\mathbb{C}} \mathsf{M}_{g,\mathbb{C}} - \dim_{\mathbb{C}} \mathsf{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}} + 1 \]
as in \autoref{Zatyplocusdef}. Applying \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop} we learn that $E^{d} = E^{d}_{r_{0}}$ is not Zariski dense in $\mathsf{M}_{g} \times \mathsf{M}_{g}$.

Now let $E = E^{d}_{r_{0}}$ be as in \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop}, and fix $([C], [C'])$ and $\beta$ as in \autoref{isogenyliftthm}. We let $w : Y \to \mathsf{A}_{g} \times \mathsf{A}_{g}$ be the Shimura variety passing through $([J(C)], [J(C')])$ and whose formal completion at $([J(C)], [J(C')])$ contains the formal deformation scheme $B := \mathrm{Def}(J(C), J(C'), \beta) \xrightarrow{w} \mathsf{A}_{g} \times \mathsf{A}_{g}$ parameterizing deformations of the Jacobians $J(C)$ and $J(C')$ together with the isogeny $\beta$. Then because $\beta$ is prime-to-$p$, the corresponding cycle class $[\beta] \in \mathrm{Hom}(H^1_{\operatorname{dR}}(C'), H^1_{\operatorname{dR}}(C))$ is an isomorphism which preserves $\mathrm{Fil}^1$. Over $B_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$, the class $[\beta]$ extends to a flat section $\widetilde{\beta}$ of ${
	\left.\kern-\nulldelimiterspace
	\operatorname{\mathscr{H}\text{\kern -3pt {\calligra\large om}}\,}(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{V})
	\vphantom{\big|}
	\right|_{B_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}}
	}$ which preserves $\mathrm{Fil}^1$, where $(\mathcal{V}, \nabla)$ is the flat algebraic de Rham vector bundle with connection lying over $\mathsf{A}_{g}$.

Now we consider the fibre product $U = (\mathsf{M}_{g} \times \mathsf{M}_{g}) \times_{\mathsf{A}_{g} \times \mathsf{A}_{g}} B$, and write $U = \mathrm{Spf} R$. Suppose that $g \leq 9$, and that the point $([C], [C']) \in U(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p})$ does not lift to a point of $U(\mathcal{O}_{K})$, where $K$ is a finite extension of $W[1/p]$ with $W = W(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p})$. Then by \cite[Lem. 2.1.5]{zbMATH08159582}, this can only happen if $R$ is not flat over $W$. 

Write $B = \mathrm{Spf}\, S$ for a complete local ring $S$. Let $Q$ be the complete local ring of $\mathsf{A}_{g} \times \mathsf{A}_{g}$ at $([J(C)], [J(C')], \beta)$. Then $S$ is a quotient of $Q$ cut out by exactly $m = g(g+1)/2$ functions, say $y_{1}, \hdots, y_{m}$. Since $g \leq 9$ we have $m < 2(3g-3)$. If $U$ is a complete local intersection in the complete local ring of $\mathsf{M}_{g} \times \mathsf{M}_{g}$ at $([C], [C'], \beta)$, then $R$ is flat by miracle flatness. It follows that $U$ is not a complete local intersection, and so 
\[ \dim U_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}} \geq 2 \dim_{\mathbb{C}} \mathsf{M}_{g,\mathbb{C}} - m + 1 = d . \]
Now consider a component $N$ of $(\mathsf{M}_{g} \times \mathsf{M}_{g})_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}} \times_{(\mathsf{A}_{g} \times \mathsf{A}_{g})_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}} Y_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$ that factors the map from $U_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$. Then $\dim N \geq d$. At a general smooth $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}$-point of $N$, we can construct an $r_{0}$-limp $\psi : \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r_{0}} \to \widecheck{D}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$ which maps to $(\beta, 1) Z_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$. It then follows that $N$ lies over $E$, and hence so does $U$. The result follows.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{monodromygrouplem}
Suppose that $\varphi : T \to \mathcal{A}_{g}$ is a complex algebraic map of Deligne-Mumford stacks such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item[-] the image of $\varphi$ contains a Hodge-generic point; and
\item[-] the image $Y$ of $T$ in $\mathsf{A}_{g}$ positive-dimensional.
\end{itemize}
Then the algebraic monodromy group of $\varphi^{*} \mathbb{V}^{\vee}$ is equal to $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By \cite[\S2.2]{zbMATH07305885} the Mumford-Tate group of a Hodge generic point in $\mathcal{A}_{g}$, and hence of a Hodge-generic point of $T(\mathbb{C})$, is $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{GSp}_{2g}$, where the semi-direct action is the natural one given by the standard representation of $\mathrm{GSp}_{2g}$. One easily checks that the derived subgroup of this Mumford-Tate group is $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$. Now by \cite[Thm. 1]{zbMATH00060857} the algebraic monodromy group of $T$ is necessarily a $\mathbb{Q}$-normal subgroup $H$ of $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$. The image $F$ of $H$ in $\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$ is normal in $\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$, and equal to the algebraic monodromy group of $Y$ in $\mathsf{A}_{g}$. Since $Y$ is positive-dimensional, the group $F$ is not the trivial group, so it follows that $F = \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$. Then $H$ is a normal subgroup of $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$ which projects onto $\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$, so necessarily equal to $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
Up to increasing $N$, the restriction of $\alpha^{d}_{r}$ from \autoref{bigjetthm} to $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}$ lands inside $J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{D}$. Correspondingly, $\eta^d_r$ factors through $\mathbf{H}_{t} \backslash J^{d}_{r} \widecheck{D}$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Since we are free to increase $N$, it suffices to show the statement when $R = \mathbb{C}$. Consider the multisection of the local system $\mathrm{Hom}(\varphi^{*} \mathbb{V}^{\vee}, (\varphi^{*} \mathbb{V}^{\vee})_{t})$ which extends the identity $\textrm{id}_{t} \in \mathrm{Hom}((\varphi^{*} \mathbb{V}^{\vee})_{t}, (\varphi^{*} \mathbb{V}^{\vee})_{t})$. Because the monodromy group is contained in $\mathbf{H}_{t}$, the image $\mathcal{F}$ in $\mathcal{P}$ of this multisection lies inside an $\mathbf{H}_{t}$-torsor, necessarily equal to $\mathcal{M}$ since $\mathcal{M}$ contains $\textrm{id}_{t}$. 

Using the description of the maps $\alpha^{d}_{r}(k)$ from \S\ref{infpermapsec}, it suffices to show that for each complex analytic period map $\psi : B \to \widecheck{L}$, with $B \subset T(\mathbb{C})$ a small complex analytic ball and where the initial condition of $\psi$ at some point $s \in T(\mathbb{C})$ corresponds to a point of $\mathcal{M}(\mathbb{C})$, factors through $\widecheck{D}$. By acting with elements $h \in \mathbf{H}_{t}(\mathbb{C})$ and replacing $\psi$ with $h \psi$, we can reduce to the case where the corresponding point from $\mathcal{M}(\mathbb{C})$ lies in $\mathcal{F}$. Then $\psi$ is a Hodge-theoretic period map in the usual sense, and the result follows from \cite[Lem. A.5]{zbMATH07973997}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{mixedatyplocusconstrprop}
Suppose that $\varphi : T \to \mathcal{A}_{g}$ is generically finite. Choose $d$ such that $\dim T_{\mathbb{C}} - d < \dim \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} - m$. Let $E^{d}_{r}(\xi)$ be the stack-theoretic image\footnote{That is, the smallest closed substack containing the usual image.} of the map $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(g)' \to T$, and set 
\begin{equation}
    \label{xiEdinteq}
    E^{d}(\xi) = \bigcap_{r \geq \xi} E^{d}_{r}(\xi) .
\end{equation} Then $E^{d}(\xi)$ is not Zariski dense in $T$, and $E^{d}(\xi)(\mathbb{C})$ lies in a finite union of special subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}}$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
We emphasize that the base $B$ of the family $g : \mathcal{F} \to B$ in the statement of \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop} is finite-type, and possibly disconnected.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
From now on we suppress the dependence on $\xi$ and write $E^{d}, E^{d}_{r}$, etc. Define $r_{0}$ analogously to \autoref{constr: atypical E}, and define 
\[ \mathcal{J}_{r_{0}} = \bigcap_{r \geq r_{0}} \textrm{im}[\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(g)' \to \mathcal{M}^{d}_{r_{0}} \times J^{d}_{r_{0}} \widecheck{D} \times B] . \]
Let $(p_{r_{0}}, \sigma_{r_{0}}, b)$ be a $\mathbb{C}$-point of $\mathcal{J}_{r_{0}}$. Let $s \in T(\mathbb{C})$ be the image of $p_{r_{0}}$. Define $\mathbb{D}^{d}_{\infty,\mathbb{C}}$ as in the proof of \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop}. Applying \cite[Lem 5.3]{zbMATH07871772} to the sequence $\{ \mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(g)' \}_{r \ge r_{0}}$ at the point $(p_{r_{0}}, \sigma_{r_{0}}, b)$ and arguing as in the proof of \cite[Prop. 4.2.5]{zbMATH08159582} we obtain a commutative diagram of formal objects
\begin{equation}
\label{Fbjetdiag}
    \begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathbb{D}^d_{\infty, \mathbb{C}}} & {\widehat{T}_s} \\
	{\mathcal{F}_{b}} & {\widecheck{D}_\mathbb{C}}
	\arrow["{j_\infty}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\sigma_\infty}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\psi_\infty}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd} .
\end{equation}
Moreover $j_{\infty}$ is injective on tangent spaces (hence an embedding), and $\sigma_{\infty}$ does not land in any fibre of $\widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} \to \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}}/W_{0}$, since its restriction to $\mathbb{D}^{d}_{\xi}$ does not by construction. Also by construction, we have, formally at $s$, that
\[ \dim \psi^{-1}_{\infty}(\mathcal{F}_{b}) \geq d > \dim T_{\mathbb{C}} + m - \dim \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} .\]
Applying the Ax-Schanuel theorem for variations of mixed Hodge structures in the abelian setting \cite{zbMATH07305885} (cf. the more general statements for variations of mixed Hodge structures in \cite{zbMATH07973997} and \cite{zbMATH07826787}), one learns that $j_{\infty}$ factors through a strict weakly special subvariety $Y$ of $T_{\mathbb{C}}$. Moreover because $\psi_{\infty} \circ j_{\infty}$ does not lie inside a fibre of $\mu$ by construction, the corresponding weakly special subvariety does not lie inside a fibre of $\mathcal{A}_{g} \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$.

Using the classification of weakly special subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_{g}$ from \cite[Prop. 1.1]{zbMATH06842935}, we learn that $Y$ necessarily maps into a strict \emph{special} subvariety of $\mathsf{A}_{g}$. These are of two types: torsion sections of $\mathcal{A}_{g} \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$, and special subvarieties not dominant over $\mathsf{A}_{g}$. This reasoning does not depend on the point of $\mathcal{J}_{r_0}$ chosen, so it follows that $E^{d}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is contained in a finite union of special subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_{g}$, strictly contained in $\mathcal{A}_{g}$.  To show that these special subvarieties pull back to strict subvarieties of $T_{\mathbb{C}}$, use \autoref{monodromygrouplem} and observe that special subvarieties have algebraic monodromy group strictly contained in $\mathbb{G}^{2g}_{a} \rtimes \mathrm{Sp}_{2g}$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2}
Suppose that the nonempty fibres of $T \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ are geometrically irreducible of dimension $e$. Choose $d$ such that $e - d < g - m$. Let $E^{d}_{r}$ be the scheme-theoretic image of the map $\mathcal{M}^{d}_{r}(g)' \to T$, and set $E^{d} = \bigcap_{r \geq 0} E^{d}_{r}$. Suppose that $\varphi : T \to \mathcal{A}_{g}$ satisfies the assumptions of \autoref{monodromygrouplem}. Then $E^{d}$ is not Zariski dense in $T$, and $E^{d}(\mathbb{C})$ lies in the union of finitely many strict special subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_{g}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Again we reduce to considering the case where $R = \mathbb{C}$. Define $r_{0}, \mathcal{J}_{r_0}, (p_{r_0}, \sigma_{r_0}, b)$ and $s$ as in the proof of \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop}. Once again we obtain a diagram of the form (\ref{Fbjetdiag}). The key difference in this case is that the map $\mathcal{F}_{b} \hookrightarrow \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}}$ factors through a fibre $F$ of the map $\widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} \to \widecheck{D}_{\mathbb{C}} / W_{0}$. Let $A$ be the fibre of $\mathcal{A}_{g} \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ which contains $s$. 

By restricting $\mathbb{V}^{\vee}$ to $A_{\mathbb{C}}$, we can consider a period map $\psi$ for this restricted VHS which is defined in some analytic neighbourhood of $s$. Then we have that 
\[ \dim (T_{\mathbb{C}} \cap A_{\mathbb{C}}) - \dim \psi^{-1}(\mathcal{F}_{b}) \leq e - d < g - m . \]
Applying the Ax-Schanuel theorem \cite{zbMATH07305885} (cf. \cite{zbMATH07973997} and \cite{zbMATH07826787}) for the variation on $T_{\mathbb{C}} \cap A_{\mathbb{C}}$ we learn that $\psi^{-1}(\mathcal{F}_{s})$ lies in a strict weakly special subvariety of $T_{\mathbb{C}} \cap A_{\mathbb{C}}$. Such subvarieties are intersections with translates of strict abelian subvarieties of $A_{\mathbb{C}}$, so this can only happen if $A_{\mathbb{C}}$ is not simple. Then in particular $s$ is not Hodge-generic (since its image in $\mathsf{A}_{g}$ is not), and $s$ lies in the intersection with $T$ of a special subvariety of $\mathcal{A}_{g}$. There are countably many such subvarieties, and $E^{d}$ is algebraic, so in fact only finitely many such special subvarieties are required to cover $E^{d}(\mathbb{C})$. Moreover since $T$ contains at least one Hodge-generic point, it follows that $E^{d}$ is not Zariski dense in $T$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{drcohomdef}
    The de Rham realization of $G$ is $\underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G) := \mathrm{Lie}(\widetilde{E}_{A})^\vee$. Note that this is a locally free sheaf of rank $2 \dim A + \mathrm{rank\,} T$ which fits into an exact sequence 
    \begin{equation}
        0 \to \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(A) \to \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G) \to \mathrm{Lie}(T)^\vee \to 0.
    \end{equation}
    We equip $\underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G)$ with an ascending weight filtration $W_0 = 0, W_{1} = \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(A)$ and $W_2 = \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G)$, and a descending Hodge filtration $F^0 = \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G), F^1 =$ annihilator of $\Omega_{A^{\vee}}$, and $F^2 =0$.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
In \S\ref{subsec: deform log 1-motif} we will discuss 1-motifs. If $Q$ is the 1-motif defined by $[0 \to G]$, then $\underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(Q) = \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G)$ except that $W_{i + 1} \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(Q) = W_{i} \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G)$. If $S$ is a separated scheme over a base $S_0$, then $\underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G)$ is moreover equipped with a Gauss-Manin connection $\nabla_{S/S_0} : \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G) \to \underline{\mathrm{H}}^1_\mathrm{dR}(G) {\otimes} \Omega_{S/S_0}$ (cf. \cite[\S1.1.3]{Mad19}).
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{immersivelem}
Away from the fibre above the hyperelliptic locus of $\mathsf{M}_{g}$, and the diagonal locus
\[ \{ ([C], x, y) \in \mathsf{M}_{g,2} : x = y \} \subset \mathsf{M}_{g,2} , \]
the map $\varphi$ is injective on tangent spaces.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
It is well known that the map $\mathsf{M}_{g} \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ is immersive away from the hyperelliptic locus. Fixing a point $[C] \in \mathsf{M}_{g}$ away from the hyperelliptic locus, it suffices to show that the map $\mathsf{M}_{g,2,[C]} \to \mathcal{A}_{g,[J(C)]}$ is injective on tangent spaces away from the diagonal locus where $x = y$. At the point $([C], x, y)$, the map on tangent spaces is given by
\[ T_{(x,y)} C^2 \ni (v_{x}, v_{y}) \mapsto ([\omega] \mapsto v_{x}(\omega) - v_{y}(\omega)) \in \mathrm{H}^0(C, \omega_C)^\vee = T_{[x - y]} J(C) . \]
Away from the hyperelliptic locus, it is well known that the map $C \to \mathbb{P}^{g-1}$ given by $x \mapsto [v_{x}] \in \mathbb{P} H^{0}(C, \omega_{C})^{\vee}$ is an embedding, so the above map can only fail to be injective when $x = y$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop: main prop mixed}
There exists a strict substack $E \subset \mathsf{M}_{g,2}$ and an integer $N$, such that 
\begin{itemize}
\item[-] $E_{\mathbb{C}} \cap \mathsf{M}^{\circ}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}}$ is a finite union of strict special subvarieties of $\mathsf{M}^{\circ}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}}$ for the restriction of the mixed VHS $\mathbb{V}^{\vee}(-1)$; and
\item[-] Suppose $0 \leq k \leq g$ is an integer such that
\begin{equation}
\label{expecteddimassump}
\dim \mathsf{M}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}} + \dim (\mathcal{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_{k})_{\mathbb{C}} \geq \dim \mathcal{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}} + 1 .
\end{equation}
Let $w : Y := \mathcal{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_k \to \mathcal{A}_g$ be the natural morphism. Then if $\gamma \in \mathrm{GSp}_{2g}(\mathbb{A}_f^p)$ and $w_\gamma : Y_\gamma \to \mathcal{A}_g$ is the Hecke translate of $w$ in the above sense, the fibre product $(\mathsf{M}_{g,2} \setminus E) \times_{\mathcal{A}_g,\varphi,w_\gamma} Y_\gamma$ is flat over $\mathbb{Z}[1/N,1/\operatorname{Ram}(T_\gamma)]$ and has the expected codimension, where $\operatorname{Ram}(T_\gamma)$ is the set of primes where the Hecke correspondence ramifies.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
For $g = 2$ the map $\mathsf{M}_{2,2} \to \mathcal{A}_{2}$ is dominant, so the result follows from basic facts about $\mathcal{A}_{2}$. We therefore assume $g \geq 3$, and so that not all curves are hyperelliptic. It suffices to prove the statement for a fixed $k$, and after replacing $\mathsf{M}_{g,2}$ with $T := \mathsf{M}^{\circ}_{g,2}$. We will then construct $E \subset T$ as a union $E_{\rightarrow} \cup E_{\uparrow}$ of atypical loci which are ``horizontal'' (along $\mathsf{A}_{g}$) and ``vertical'' (along the fibres of $\mathcal{A}_{g} \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$). This we will do via applications of \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop} and \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2}, respectively. 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           

We recall the description of the algebraic variety $\widecheck{D}$ in \cite[\S2.5]{zbMATH07305885}, where it is called $\mathcal{X}^{\vee}$. From \cite[Ex. 2.9]{zbMATH07305885} and the fact that the variety $\mathcal{X}^{\vee}$ is a quotient of the group $P(\mathbb{C})$ in \cite[\S2.5]{zbMATH07305885}, one deduces that $\widecheck{D}$ is a rank $g$ complex vector bundle over $\widecheck{D}/W_0$, and that $\widecheck{D}/W_0$ is the usual symplectic Grassmannian that compactifies the Siegel upper half space. Now observe that $\widecheck{D}$ sits naturally inside the Grassmannian of $g$-dimensional Lagrangian subspaces of the fixed fibre $\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{t}$. Since $\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{t}$ has rank $2g+1$, this space has dimension $g(g+1)/2 + g$, hence contains $\widecheck{D}$ as a Zariski open subset. 

To apply \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2} we construct a family $g : \mathcal{F} \to B$ of algebraic subvarieties of $\widecheck{D}$ as follows. The base $B$ we take to be $\widecheck{D}/W_{0} \times \operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{t}, 2k)$. Given a point $(F, \alpha) \in B$, where $F = \mathrm{Fil}^1 + W_{0}$, the fibre $g^{-1}(F, \alpha)$ is the locus of all choices of $\mathrm{Fil}^1$ such that $\mathrm{Fil}^1 + W_{0} = F$ and $\dim \mathrm{Fil}^1 \cap \alpha = k$. We write $E_{\uparrow}$ for the locus from \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2} associated to $g$, and set $E = E_{\rightarrow} \cup E_{\uparrow}$; we choose $d$ to be
\[ d := \dim \mathsf{M}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}} + \dim (\mathcal{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_{k})_{\mathbb{C}} - \dim \mathcal{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}} + 1 . \]

To apply \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop} we construct a family $g : \mathcal{F} \to B$ of algebraic subschemes of $\widecheck{D}$ over $R = \mathbb{Z}[1/N]$ that contains the algebraic varieties corresponding to all the Hecke translates $w_\gamma : Y_\gamma \to \mathcal{A}_g$ in the statement. For the base $B$ we take $\mathrm{Sp}_{2g} \times \operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{t}, 2k)$, where the second factor parametrizes subspaces of $\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{t}$ of dimension $2k$. Let $\widecheck{E} \subset \widecheck{D}/W_{0}$ be the flag subscheme corresponding to $\mathsf{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_{k}$. Then the fibres of $g$ are of the form
\[ g^{-1}(h, \alpha) = \{ \mathrm{Fil}^1 \in \widecheck{D} : \mathrm{Fil}^1 + W_0 \in h \widecheck{E}, \hspace{1em} \dim \mathrm{Fil}^1 \cap \alpha = k \} . \]
After removing a constructible locus from the base $B$ and reparameterizing, we may assume that the fibres of $g$ all have the same dimension as $Y_\gamma$. The descending chain $E^d_r$ from \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2} stabilizes, so we choose $\xi$ such that $E_{\uparrow}=E^d_{\xi}$. We then use this $\xi$ in  \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop} and write $E_{\rightarrow}$ for the locus associated to the present family $g$ and this value of $\xi$; we choose the same $d$ as before. Note that the intersection in (\ref{xiEdinteq}) stabilizes at some $r_{0} \geq \xi$ which can be larger than $\xi$.

Now consider the fibre product
\begin{equation}
    \label{Stkeq}
    S_{\gamma,k} := T \times_{\mathcal{A}_g,\varphi,w_\gamma} Y_\gamma .
\end{equation}
Suppose that $S_{\gamma,k}$ is non-empty and contains a point $s$ lying over $\mathbb{Z}[1/N,1/\operatorname{Ram}(T_\gamma)]$ at which $S_{\gamma,k}$ is not flat, and write $x \in T$ and $y \in Y_\gamma$ for the images of $s$. It suffices to assume that $s$ is a closed point whose residue characteristic $p$ does not divide $N$ or $\operatorname{Ram}(T_\gamma)$, and that $p > r_{0}$. Away from these primes $p_1$ and $p_2$ are \'etale, so the morphism $w_\gamma : Y_\gamma \to \mathcal{A}_g$ is a local complete intersection of the expected codimension. Hence the lack of flatness implies, by miracle flatness, that $S_{\gamma,k}$ has bigger than expected dimension modulo $p$ at $s$, i.e.
\begin{align*}
\dim_x T_{\kappa(s)} - \dim_s S_{\gamma,k,\kappa(s)} &< \dim_{w_\gamma(y)} \mathcal{A}_{g,\kappa(s)} - \dim_y (Y_\gamma)_{\kappa(s)} .
\end{align*}
From our assumption (\ref{expecteddimassump}), one deduces that $\dim_{s} S_{\gamma,k,\kappa(s)} \geq d \geq 2$. Let $C$ be a component of $S_{\gamma,k,\kappa(s)}$ passing through $s$ satisfying $\dim C \geq d$. There are now two options.

Let $f : C^{\mathrm{red}} \to \mathsf{A}_g$ be the composite of $C^{\mathrm{red}} \to \mathcal{A}_g$ with the projection $\mathcal{A}_g \to \mathsf{A}_g$. Suppose first that, at a general smooth point $s \in C^{\mathrm{red}}$, there exists a non-degenerate $d$-jet $j_{\xi} : \mathbb{D}^d_{\xi,\kappa(s)} \to C^{\mathrm{red}}$ such that $J^d_{\xi}f(j_{\xi})$ is non-constant. Fix any $r \geq r_{0}$, with $r < p$, and extend $j_{\xi}$ to a non-degenerate $r$-jet $j : \mathbb{D}^d_{r,\kappa(s)} \to C^{\mathrm{red}}$. We take $p$ to be any point of the torsor $\mathcal{M}$ above $s$. Then $\alpha(j,p)$ is a non-degenerate jet in $J^d_r \widecheck{D}_{\kappa(s)}$ whose image in $J^d_r (\widecheck{D}/W_{0})_{\kappa(s)}$ is non-constant at order $\xi$. To show that $s$ lies in $E^d_r(\xi)$, it therefore suffices to construct $b$ such that $\alpha(j,p) \in J^{d}_{r} g^{-1}(b)$.

To find such a $b$ it suffices to show that the data $(j^{*} \mathcal{H}^{\vee}, j^{*} W_{\bullet}, j^{*} \mathrm{Fil}^{\bullet}, j^{*} \nabla)$ admits:
\begin{itemize}
    \item a flat idempotent $c : j^{*} \mathcal{H}^{\vee}/W_{0} \to j^{*} \mathcal{H}^{\vee}/W_{0}$ which splits the filtered vector bundle $(j^{*} \mathcal{H}^{\vee}/W_{0}, \mathrm{Fil}^{\bullet})$ as a direct sum of summands $\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{1} \oplus \mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{2}$ of rank $2k$ and $2(g-k)$, compatibly with the polarizing form; and
    \item a flat subbundle $\alpha$ of $j^{*} \mathcal{H}^{\vee}$ of rank $2k$ such that $\mathrm{Fil}^1 \cap \alpha$ is a vector subbundle of rank $k$;
\end{itemize}
and such that the locus of flags $F^{\bullet}$ in $\widecheck{D}_{\kappa(s)}$ corresponding to $(c_{s}, \alpha_{s})$ under the map $p$ has the correct dimension. 

Recall that we have a universal semiabelian family $u$ over $\mathcal{A}_g$. The pullback $w_\gamma^{*}u$ to $Y_\gamma$ is prime-to-$p$ isogenous to a semiabelian family of the form $G \times A'$, where $G$ is semiabelian of toric rank one and $A'$ is abelian of dimension $k$. In particular, pulling back further along the morphism $j : \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)} \to C \to S_{\gamma,k} \to Y_\gamma$, we obtain a split semiabelian family, prime-to-$p$-isogenous to $j^{*} \varphi^{*}u$, which is of the form $u' : G_s \times A'_s \times \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)} \to \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)}$. The idempotent $c$ comes from the splitting up to prime-to-$p$ isogeny of the abelian part of the family $u'$. The subbundle $\alpha$ on the other hand is the kernel of 
\[ H^{1}_{\operatorname{dR}}(G_{s} \times A'_{s} \times \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)}/\mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)})^{\vee} \to H^{1}_{\operatorname{dR}}(G_{s} \times \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)} / \mathbb{D}^{d}_{r,\kappa(s)})^{\vee} \]
where the universal vector extensions are as in \autoref{drcohomdef}. To check the dimension property for the fibre at $s$, we argue as follows. The condition that $\mathrm{Fil}^1_{s}/W_{0}$ is decomposes as a direct sum into two symplectic subspaces, which are $k$ and $(g-k)$-dimensional subspaces of the images of $c$ and $1-c$, defines a subvariety of the sympletic Grassmannian of $\mathcal{H}^{\vee}_{t}/W_{0}$ of the same dimension as $\mathsf{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_{k}$. The fibre of $\widecheck{D}$ above $\mathrm{Fil}^1_{s} / W_{0}$ has dimension $g$, and its points correspond to a choice of $g$-dimensional subspace of the $g+1$-dimensional vector space $\mathrm{Fil}^1_{s} + W_{0}$. If such a choice intersects the kernel $K$ of $H^{1}_{\operatorname{dR}}(G_{s} \times A'_{s})^{\vee} \to H^{1}_{\operatorname{dR}}(G_{s})^{\vee}$ in a subspace of dimension $k$ then it is uniquely determined by its image in $H^{1}_{\operatorname{dR}}(G_{s})^{\vee}$. The remaining freedom in choosing this image is a variety of dimension $g-k$. We conclude that $s \in E^d_r(\xi)$. Since we chose $r \geq r_{0}$, $s \in E_{\rightarrow}$. This holds at a general point of $C$, and $E_{\rightarrow}$ is closed, so $C \subset E_{\rightarrow}$; in particular our original point lies in $E_{\rightarrow}$.

Suppose instead that at a general smooth point $s \in C^{\mathrm{red}}$ every non-degenerate $d$-jet $j_{\xi} : \mathbb{D}^d_{\xi,\kappa(s)} \to C^{\mathrm{red}}$ has constant image in $\mathsf{A}_g$ to order $\xi$. Choose such a jet and a point $p$ of the torsor $\mathcal{M}$ above $s$. Since $T=\mathsf{M}^\circ_{g,2}$ and $j_{\xi}$ is non-degenerate, its full period $1$-jet is non-constant. The same splitting data coming from the Hecke source places $\alpha(j_{\xi},p)$ in a fibre of the family used to define the loci $E^d_r$ in \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2}. Hence $s \in E^d_{\xi}=E_{\uparrow}$, and therefore $C \subset E_{\uparrow}$. Notice that this argument does not require $C$ itself to lie in a fibre of $\mathcal{A}_g \to \mathsf{A}_g$; it only uses that its $d$-jets of order $\xi$ have constant image in $\mathsf{A}_g$. The numerical hypothesis of \autoref{mixedatyplocusconstrprop2} is the same as before: here $m \leq g-1$ and $e=2$, so it is enough that $d>1$, which holds for an unexpected component under \eqref{expecteddimassump}.

We have shown that all unexpected components of the loci $S_{\gamma,k,\kappa(s)}$ lie in the locus $E = E_{\rightarrow} \cup E_{\uparrow}$. Flatness away from $E$ now follows as usual from miracle flatness, as does the expected dimension condition (by construction).
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor: intersect with torsion}
Let $\mathbf{g}$ be a partition of $g$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{atypintineqMg2}
\delta(\mathbf{g}) + (g-g_{k}) \leq \dim \mathsf{M}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}} - 1 ,
\end{equation}
and let $T_j$ be an \'etale scheme over $\mathsf{A}_{g_j}$. Suppose $T := \prod_j T_j$ is equipped with a morphism $T \to \mathsf{A}_g$ and that
$$\psi : \prod_{j = 1}^k \mathcal{A}_{g_j}|_{T_j} \to \mathcal{A}_{g}|_T$$
is a prime-to-$p$ symplectic similitude. Assume $n \in \mathcal{O}_T^\times$ and the image of $T$ is disjoint from the image of $E$ in $\mathcal{A}_g$. Then the fiber product$$\mathsf{M}_{g, 2} \times_{\mathcal{A}_g} \Big[ \big( \prod_{j = 1}^{k - 1} \mathcal{A}_{g_j}|_{T_j} \big)[n] \times \mathcal{A}_{g_k} \Big]$$ is flat over $\mathbb{Z}$ and has the expected codimension $\delta(\mathbf{g}) + (g - g_k)$ in $\mathsf{M}_{g, 2}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{Hinjlem}
For any point $q = ([C], p, \iota(p)) \in \mathsf{H}_{g,2}$ defined over a field of characteristic $\neq 2$, the induced map on tangent spaces $T_{q} \mathsf{H}_{g,2} \to T_{\varphi(q)} \mathcal{A}_{g}$ is injective.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Let $\pi : \mathsf{H}_{g,2} \to \mathsf{H}_{g}$ be the obvious projection. By \cite[Thm. 1.2]{zbMATH07346761} the maps $T_{\pi(q)} \mathsf{H}_{g} \to T_{\tau(\pi(q))} \mathsf{A}_{g}$ are injective, where $\tau : \mathsf{H}_{g} \to \mathsf{A}_{g}$ is the usual map. It therefore suffices to pass to the fibres above $\pi(q)$ and $\tau(\pi(q))$ and verify that the maps $T_{(p, \iota(p))} C^{\iota} \to T_{p - \iota(p)} J(C)$ are injective, where $C^{\iota} \subset C^2$ is the locus of points $(x, y) \in C^2$ such that $y = \iota(x)$.

The map on tangent spaces is then
\[ T_{(p, \iota(p))} C^{\iota} \ni (v_{p}, \iota(v_{p})) \mapsto ([\omega] \mapsto v_{p}(\omega) - v_{p}(\iota^{*} \omega)) \in H^{0}(C, \omega_{C})^{\vee} = T_{[p - \iota(p)]} J(C) . \]
This map is injective provided that $\omega - \iota^{*} \omega$ does not vanish at $p$ for all $\omega$. But $\iota$ acts on the standard hyperelliptic forms $x^{i} dx / y$ by multiplication by $(-1)$, so $\omega - \iota^{*} \omega = 2 \omega$ which is non-zero in characteristic not equal to $2$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop: main prop mixed2}
There exists a strict subscheme $E \subset \mathsf{H}_{g,2}$ and an integer $N$, such that 
\begin{itemize}
\item[-] $E_{\mathbb{C}} \cap \mathsf{H}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}}$ is a finite union of strict special subvarieties of $\mathsf{H}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}}$ for the restriction of the mixed VHS $\mathbb{V}^{\vee}(-1)$; and
\item[-] Suppose $0 \leq k \leq g$ is an integer such that

                                        
\begin{equation}
\dim \mathsf{H}_{g,2,\mathbb{C}} + \dim (\mathcal{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_{k})_{\mathbb{C}} \geq \dim \mathcal{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}} .
\end{equation}
Let $w : Y := \mathcal{A}_{g-k} \times \mathsf{A}_k \to \mathcal{A}_g$ be the natural morphism.
