    The caveat is that the discriminant locus of $\mathsf{M}$ parametrizing the singular fibers is a divisor, and remains a divisor in $\mathsf{M}'$. Let us call this divisor $\mathsf{D}$. As resolving RDP singularities incurs exceptional divisors on the resolved surfaces, $\mathsf{D}$ is an atypical component of the Noether-Lefschetz locus. There is a possibility that $\mathsf{D}$ is contained in $E$, so that there is no added generality. However, where $\mathsf{D}$ is contained in $D$ can in principle be decided effectively (cf. \cref{rmk: effectivity}).
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop: alternating}
    Let $k$ be a field. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape{(\alph*)}]
        \item An alternating form $(V, \omega)$ over $k$ is classified up to isometry by $\dim V$ and $\dim \mathrm{Rad}(\omega)$. Furthermore, the induced alternating form on the quotient $V / \mathrm{Rad}(\omega)$ is always symplectic (i.e., non-degenerate).  
        \item Let $(V, \omega)$ be a symplectic space and let $M_1, M_2 \subseteq V$ be subspaces. There exists $\gamma \in \mathrm{Sp}(V, \omega)$ such that $\gamma(M_1) = M_2$ if and only if $\dim M_1 = \dim M_2$ and $\dim \mathrm{Rad}(\omega|_{M_1}) = \dim \mathrm{Rad}(\omega|_{M_2})$. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Part (a) is standard, and (b) follows from (a) by Witt's cancellation theorem for symplectic forms (see e.g., \cite{James}, which holds over any PID).
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop: isotropic in M}
    Let $(M, \omega)$ be an alternating space of dimension $2m$ over a field $k$, and let $R = \mathrm{Rad}(\omega)$ have dimension $2r$. The variety $X = \mathrm{IGr}(m, M)$ of $m$-dimensional isotropic subspaces admits a locally closed stratification
    $$ X = \bigsqcup_{j = r}^{\min(m, 2r)} X_j, $$
    where $X_j = \{ W \in X \mid \dim(W \cap R) = j \}$. Each stratum $X_j$ is an affine bundle of rank $(m-j)(2r-j)$ over $\mathrm{Gr}(j, R) \times \mathrm{IGr}(m-j, M/R)$, and has dimension
    $$ \dim X_j = \frac{1}{2}m(m+1) + 2jr - \frac{1}{2}j(3j+1). $$
    Moreover, $X$ is irreducible with the unique open dense stratum being $X_r$. In particular, 
    $$ \dim X = \dim X_r = \frac{1}{2}m(m+1) + \frac{1}{2}r(r-1). $$
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Let $\bar{M} = M/R$ be the symplectic quotient, which has dimension $2m-2r$. The natural projection $\pi \colon M \to \bar{M}$ maps $W \in X_j$ to an isotropic subspace $\bar{W} \subset \bar{M}$ of dimension $m-j$. The isotropy of $\bar{W}$ forces $m-j \le (\dim \bar{M})/2 = m-r$, giving the lower bound $j \ge r$.
    
    A subspace $W \in X_j$ is uniquely determined by the choices of the intersection $K = W \cap R \in \mathrm{Gr}(j, R)$, and a linear complement to $R \cap W$ in $W$. It is easy to check that the natural map $X_j \to \mathrm{Gr}(j, R) \times \mathrm{IGr}(m-j, \bar{M})$ given by sending $W$ to $(K, \bar{W})$ is surjective. Fixing $K$ and $\bar{W}$, the space of subspaces $W \subset \pi^{-1}(\bar{W})$ satisfying $W \cap R = K$ and mapping surjectively onto $\bar{W}$ is a torsor under $\mathrm{Hom}(\bar{W}, R/K)$. This affine space has dimension $\dim(\bar{W}) \dim(R/K) = (m-j)(2r-j)$, yielding the desired fibration.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem: Z_M}
    Let $(V, \omega)$ be a symplectic space of dimension $2g$, and let $M \subseteq V$ be a subspace of dimension $2m \le g$. Set $2r = \dim \mathrm{Rad}(\omega|_M)$. Let $Z_M \subseteq \mathrm{IGr}(g, V)$ be the subvariety defined by 
    $$ Z_M = \{ F \in \mathrm{IGr}(g, V) \mid \dim (F \cap M) = m \}. $$
    Then $Z_M$ is an irreducible variety in $\mathrm{IGr}(g, V)$ of codimension
    \begin{align*}
        s(g, m, r) &= \frac{1}{2}g(g + 1) - \big[ \frac{1}{2}m(m+1) + \frac{1}{2}r(r-1) + \frac{1}{2}(g-m)(g-m+1) \big] \\
        &= m(g-m)-\frac{r(r-1)}2. 
    \end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Consider the projection $\phi \colon Z_M \to \mathrm{IGr}(m, M)$ given by $F \mapsto F \cap M$. For any $E \in \mathrm{IGr}(m, M)$, the fiber $\phi^{-1}(E)$ consists of Lagrangians $F \subset V$ containing $E$ such that $F \cap M = E$. Passing to the symplectic quotient $E^\perp/E$, these correspond exactly to Lagrangians in $E^\perp/E$ that trivially intersect the $m$-dimensional subspace $M/E$. Since the symplectic quotient has dimension $2(g-m)$ and $2m \le g$, a generic Lagrangian in $E^\perp/E$ intersects $M/E$ trivially. Thus, the fibers of $\phi$ are non-empty, Zariski open dense subvarieties of the Lagrangian Grassmannian $\mathrm{IGr}(g-m, E^\perp/E)$. The dimension formula now follows from \cref{prop: isotropic in M}.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop: strict filtered}
    Let $S$ be any base scheme. If $0 \to B \to A \to Q \to 0$ is an exact sequence of abelian schemes over $S$, then the induced sequence $0 \to \mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(Q/S) \to \mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(A/S) \to \mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(B/S) \to 0$ is also exact and strict (\cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0123}{Tag 0123}]{stacks-project}) as a sequence of filtered vector bundles.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
For any abelian scheme $\pi_X \colon X \to S$ with zero section $e_S$, the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$, providing a canonical short exact sequence of vector bundles
    $$ 0 \to \omega_{X/S} \to \mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(X/S) \to R^1\pi_{X,*}\mathcal{O}_X \to 0, $$
    which defines the Hodge filtration. Moreover, there are canonical identifications $\mathrm{Lie}(X/S) \simeq e_S^* \Omega_{X/S}^\vee$ and $\mathrm{Lie}(X^\vee /S) \simeq R^1\pi_{X,*}\mathcal{O}_X$ (\cite[\S8.4~Thm.~1]{BLR}). The statement then follows from the fact that $X \mapsto \mathrm{Lie}(X/S)$ and $X \mapsto X^\vee$ are both exact functors on abelian schemes.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
Let $(A, \lambda)$ be a principally polarized abelian variety over a field $k$ and $B \subseteq A$ be an abelian subvariety. We define the Artin invariant of the pair $(B, A, \lambda)$ to be 
    \begin{equation}
        \sigma_0(B, A, \lambda) = \frac{1}{2} \dim_k \mathrm{Rad}(\omega_{\lambda}|_{\mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(Q/k)}), \textit{ where } Q = A/B. 
    \end{equation}
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- notation-2: body_md -->
Given a scheme $S$, we write $S_{\mathrm{pos}}$ for the set of those points which are of positive transcendence degree over their prime field.
<!-- end notation-2 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem: separable}
    Let $A$ be an abelian variety over any field $k$. Every abelian subvariety $B$ of $A_{\bar{k}}$ descends to $A_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Whether or not the inclusion $B \hookrightarrow A_{\bar{k}}$ admits a splitting, there is always some $\alpha \in \mathrm{End}(A_{\bar{k}})$ such that $B = \alpha(A_{\bar{k}})$. Then apply the well known fact that $\mathrm{End}(A_{\bar{k}}) = \mathrm{End}(A_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}})$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{thm: contains sub}
In $\mathsf{A}_g$ consider the locus
$$\mathcal{S}(m,\sigma_0)=\{x\in\mathsf{A}_{g,\mathrm{pos}}:\mathcal{A}_{\bar{x}}\text{ admits an abelian subvariety $B$ with }\dim B=g-m\text{ and }\sigma_0(B,\mathcal{A}_{\bar{x}},\lambda_{\bar{x}})=\sigma_0\}.$$
Let $T\subseteq\mathsf{A}_g$ be a Hodge-generic locally closed subscheme whose generic fibre $T_{\mathbb{C}}$ has dimension $\leq s(g,m,\sigma_0)$, and let $E_{m,\sigma_0}\subseteq T$ be the atypical locus of type with respect to $Z_{m, \sigma_0}$, defined as in \autoref{Zatyplocusdef}. Then
$(T\cap\mathcal{S}(m,\sigma_0))_{\mathrm{pos}}\subseteq E_{m,\sigma_0}.$ If moreover the monodromy group of $T$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-simple, then $(T\cap\mathcal{S}(m,\sigma_0))_{\mathrm{pos}}$ is contained in finitely many strict Shimura subvarieties.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Each component of $(T \cap \mathcal{S}(m, \sigma_0))_{\mathrm{pos}}$ either intersects the non-empty open locus where $T$ is smooth (over $\mathrm{Spec}\, \mathbb{Z}$), or lies in a strict closed locus. By replacing $T$ with an open subscheme, we may reduce to the case where $T$ is smooth.
    
    Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the symplectic frame bundle over $\mathsf{A}_g$ whose points are given by $(x, b)$ where $x \in \mathsf{A}_g$ and $b$ is a symplectic identification $(V, \omega) {\otimes} k(x) \simeq (\mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(\mathcal{A}_{x}), \omega_{\lambda_x})$. Then for all $d$ and $r$, we have a morphism $\alpha^d_r : \mathcal{P}^d_r \to J^d_r \widecheck{D}$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/r!]$, constructed as in \autoref{refinedjetthm}.

    Suppose now that $x \in \mathcal{S}(m, \sigma_0)$. Let $S$ be the Zariski closure of $x$. Set $k = \kappa(x)$. By \cref{lem: separable}, the embedding $B \subseteq \mathcal{A}_{\bar{x}}$ is defined over $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$, so that we can find an \'etale morphism $S' \to S$ such that $B$ descends and spreads out to an abelian subscheme $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathcal{A}_{S'}$. 

                                                             

                                                         
    
    Let $x_0$ be a general point on $S$, and $\widetilde{x}_0 \in S'$ be a lift. We now claim the existence of a non-degenerate jet $\mathbb{D}^1_{r, k(x_0)} \to \mathsf{A}_g$ that lifts to $\mathcal{M}^1_r \times_{J^1_r \widecheck{D}} J^1_r Z_{m, \sigma_0}$. By \cref{prop: alternating}(b), for some choice of $b : (V, \omega) {\otimes} k(\widetilde{x}_0) \simeq (\mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(\mathcal{A}_{\widetilde{x}_0}), \omega_{\lambda_{\widetilde{x}_0}})$, $M$ is sent isometrically to $\mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(\mathcal{Q}_{\widetilde{x}_0}) \subseteq \mathrm{H}^1_\mathrm{dR}(\mathcal{A}_{\widetilde{x}_0})$ for $\mathcal{Q} := \mathcal{A}_{S'} / \mathcal{B}$. Then it follows from \cref{prop: strict filtered} that the induced local period morphism at $\widetilde{x}_0$ takes values in $Z_M \subseteq \widecheck{D}$. Since the map $S' \to S$ is \'etale, this jet remains non-degenerate after projection to $S$. 

    Now apply \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop} as follows. The embedding $\iota : L \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is the obvious embedding $\mathbb{Q} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$. The triple $(\mathcal{H}, \mathrm{Fil}^{\bullet}, \nabla)$ is that associated to the de Rham cohomology of the universal abelian scheme over $\mathsf{A}_{g}$ in degree one. The Hodge datum $(G, \Omega) = (\mathrm{GSp}_{2g}, \mathbb{H}_{g})$. We take $Z = Z_{m, \sigma_0}$. Then $j = 1$ and $I_Z^c = \varnothing$, hence $D_{Z}$ is a point. In particular $n(I) = \dim T_{\mathbb{C}}$, $\Omega' = \Omega$ and $\widecheck{D}^{\mathrm{nc}}_Z = \widecheck{D}$. The right-hand side of the inequality of \autoref{atyplocusconstrprop} then reads $\dim T_{\mathbb{C}} + \dim Z_{m, \sigma_0,\mathbb{C}} - \dim \mathsf{A}_{g,\mathbb{C}}$; by assumption this is less than $d := 1$. Then setting $E = E^{d}$, we obtain a strict Zariski closed locus $E \subset T$. By construction the jets from the previous paragraph lie above $E$, so the result follows.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{supnotdensecor}
    Let $\mathcal{S}_g \subseteq \mathsf{A}_g$ be the locus of all supersingular abelian varieties (in all characteristics). Then for each $g \ge 16$, we have that away from finitely many primes, $\mathcal{S}_{g, \mathrm{pos}} \cap \tau(\mathcal{M}_g)$ is contained in finitely many strict Shimura subvarieties of $\mathsf{A}_{g}$.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Note that $s(g, m, r)$ achieves its minimum when $r = m$. For fixed $g$, $s(g, m, m)$ is a quadratic polynomial in $m$ and achieves its maximum at $m = \lfloor (g + 1)/3 \rfloor$. Taking this $m$, whenever $g \ge 16$ we have $3g - 3 \le s(g,m, m)$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex: Artin-Schreier}
    If $\mathbb{F}_q$ is a finite field of characteristic $p$ and $R(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ is an additive polynomial of degree $p^h$, then the curve 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eqn: Artin-Scheier}
        Y: y^p - y = xR(x)
    \end{equation}
    is supersingular and has a genus $g = p^h(p-1)/2$ (\cite{vdGvdV92, Bla12, BHM+16}). Here $R[x]$ is said to be additive if $R(x_1 + x_2) = R(x_1) + R(x_2)$, or equivalently, $R(x)$ is a linear combination of monomials $x^d$, where $d$ is a power of $p$. Clearly, such families are positive-dimensional. Our \autoref{supnotdensecor} says that, when $g \geq 16$, one cannot expect to find a Zariski dense collection of positive-dimensional families of supersingular curves in $\mathsf{M}_{g}$ if one considers all primes $p$ at once. This in some sense explains why $p$ must be a function of $g$ in this example.
<!-- end example-1 -->
